Telos is the general agent execution layer of the SSCCS stack and the
base system agent instance under the actus hub. Under
[kineTics](https://docs.ssccs.org/projects/kinetics/), actus supervises
the agent executor type; Telos is its first instance. Planning with the
LLM and converting plans into system effects happen inside Telos: a
command arrives over the actus contract, a coordinate is resolved, a
process or file or network effect happens, and the result returns. The
layer is general: it is not tied to a code editor, a language, or a
domain. It executes.

The working thesis is that an agent does not need to traverse trees to
act. Files are not found by descent; work is addressed by coordinate and
reached by teleport. The agent moves between work locations in space, and
telos materializes that movement as concrete system calls, tool
invocations, and protocol traffic over files, processes, and networks.

## Layers

| Layer | Project | Role |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Physical foundation | Chton (tagma) | coordinates over disk, RAM, and network bytes |
| Data hub | Nexus | logs, snapshots, and state over the coordinate space |
| Verification | EV and peers | mathematical verification of coordinate operations |
| Agent hub | Actus | hub of the agent executor type under kineTics; supervises agent instances |
| Base agent instance | Telos | LLM planning, command intake, and system-effect conversion over ACP/MCP |

## Contract

Telos keeps a wire contract 1:1 with actus. Actus launches telos as its
agent binary (`tel`); telos connects back over WebSocket, announces readiness, and
then serves commands and emits events. The contract is the only stable
boundary: eight event types flow from telos to actus, three command types
flow from actus to telos, and every consumer path in actus depends on
their semantics, including cumulative content overwrite, turn-end replay
filtering, and the one-terminal-event-per-request rule.

The bootstrap starts at the boundary. A deterministic stub emits the
exact event sequences actus expects, the conformance suite gates every
change, and the real execution core is filled in behind that stable
surface. Because the interface is fixed first, the internals can be
rebuilt freely without touching actus.

## Design

- Command intake: chat submission, cancellation, tool authorization
  resolution arrive over the WebSocket contract.
- Coordinate resolution: work locations are addressed by tagma
  coordinates rather than path traversal, so opening a location is a jump,
  not a walk.
- Execution: file, process, network, and MCP effects are produced from
  resolved coordinates; results stream back as cumulative entries.
- Verification: EV and peers check the coordinate operations that
  execution depends on.

## Status

The contract is implemented end to end and pinned by conformance suites.
A deterministic stub backend exercises the actus flows without an LLM,
and the live suite runs through the actus `run.sh` test path. The real
agent core is attached: the `tel` binary wires the agent core and serves
the actus contract directly. Telos is an independent project; the
absorbed agent core sits beneath its own crate, and actus depends on
telos only.

Two integration items sit on the telos board: the headless entry point
must consume `--user-data-dir` so actus-injected settings and context
servers reach the agent process, and a prebuilt agent image must be
published so downstream actus CI can pull it instead of building.

Indexing into the tagma coordinate space and time teleport remain the
next steps.

## Direction

- Consume `--user-data-dir` in the headless entry point and publish the
  prebuilt agent image, completing the actus integration contract.
- Indexing integrated into tagma coordinates, so location resolution is
  arithmetic over coordinates instead of filesystem descent.
- Time teleport: nexus replay restores a previous execution state at fine
  granularity, coarser than a commit and cheaper than a checkout.
- Wider system-effect coverage across files, processes, networks, and
  MCP servers behind the fixed contract.
- The layer stays general: any LLM, any environment, any domain.
